page.overview:
What is Harfoots?

Harfoots were one of the three breeds of hobbits in Middle-earth, along with Stoors and Fallohides.

The Harfoots were the most common and typical of the Hobbits, and in later days their traits were seen as the "norm". They were shorter and smaller than other kinds, almost never growing beards and wearing no footwear. Their hands and feet were neat and nimble, and they were browner of skin. They lived in highlands and hillsides, delving tunnels, burrows or holes they called smials, a habit they instituted and maintained for the entire Third Age and beyond. They were accustomed to inhabiting one location for a long time before moving. They were the most rustic and pastoral in nature, being gifted in the arts of tilling, farming and handicrafts. The race they had the most interactions with were the Dwarves, who they were very friendly with.

In their earliest known history, the Harfoots dwelt in the central Vales of Anduin, specifically the lower foothills of the Misty Mountains. The Gladden Fields approximated their southern boundary, and a woodland of the Great Shelf, near the High Pass, was their northern boundary. In unspecified ways, the Harfoots were frequently involved with Dwarves traveling through the High Pass in the early Third Age.

The Harfoots were the first to migrate westward into Arnor, and there the Dúnedain named them Periannath or halflings, as recorded in Arnorian records around TA 1050. They tended to settle down for extended periods, founding villages as far from the Vales of Anduin as the hills of the South Downs.
